chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man sets out during the month of Ramadan after midday, he should complete his fast; and when he sets out before midday, he should break his fast.

key_terms.الزَّوَال: Midday (when the sun passes its zenith)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for a traveler who leaves home after midday during Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the precise moment of departure (Zawal) that determines whether a traveler must complete the current day's fast or may break it, reflecting the juristic consensus on the validity of the fast based on the state of the body at noon. It highlights the practical application of the concession (rukhsah) for travelers, emphasizing that the intention to travel prior to Zawal does not automatically invalidate the fast unless the physical departure occurs before the midpoint of the day. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the obligations of the resident and the privileges of the traveler during Ramadan.
